question_text: A 45-year-old woman, suspected of having colon cancer, is advised to undergo a contrast-CT scan of the abdomen. She has no comorbidities and no significant past medical history. There is also no history of drug allergy. However, she reports that she is allergic to certain kinds of seafood. After tests confirm normal renal function, she is taken to the CT scan room where radiocontrast dye is injected intravenously and a CT scan of her abdomen is conducted. While being transferred to her ward, she develops generalized itching and urticarial rashes, with facial angioedema. She becomes dyspneic. Her pulse is 110/min, the blood pressure is 80/50 mm Hg, and the respirations are 30/min. Her upper and lower extremities are pink and warm. What is the most appropriate management of this patient?
